title: Pioneering Biomedical Engineering: The Top 20 Innovative Organ-on-a-Chip Companies in 2026
summary: Top innovative organ on a chip companies in world for 2026: 20 firms like Emulate, Mimetas and TissUse, their platforms, leaders and what it means for drug R&D.

## TL;DR


- Organ-on-a-chip devices are microfluidic chips lined with living human cells that mimic how an organ works, used for drug testing, toxicology and disease modeling.
- Grand View Research projects the organ-on-a-chip market to reach $952.4 million by 2030, growing 35.11% a year from 2025 to 2030.
- This list covers 20 of the top innovative organ on a chip companies in world, including Emulate, Mimetas, TissUse and 28bio (formerly AxoSim).
- Many of these firms combine microfluidics, stem cells, sensors and AI to make preclinical testing more predictive and reduce reliance on animal models.

### What is Biomedical Engineering?


Biomedical engineering is an interdisciplinary field. It applies engineering principles to biology and medicine to improve healthcare. The field develops medical devices, imaging systems, biomaterials and bioinformatics tools. These tools help to diagnose, treat and prevent diseases. Organ-on-a-chip (OoC) technology is one important application. It simulates the functions of human organs. It gives an alternative to traditional cell cultures and animal tests.


## Understanding Organ-on-a-Chip Technology


An organ-on-a-chip is a microfluidic device. It contains living human cells in small channels. The device mimics the physical and mechanical conditions of a human organ. Researchers use these devices for drug screening, toxicology tests and disease models. Organ-on-a-chip systems are also called microphysiological systems (MPS).


The market for these devices grows quickly. Grand View Research projects that the global organ-on-a-chip market will reach USD 952.4 million by 2030. It projects a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 35.11% from 2025 to 2030 ([Grand View Research, October 2024](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/press-release/global-organ-on-a-chip-market) ). Pharmaceutical companies, biotech startups and[preclinical CROs](https://www.scispot.com/blog/digital-transformation-in-preclinical-cros-why-the-time-to-act-is-now) use these systems. For more companies that change biotechnology, read about[10 innovative venture-backed companies](https://www.scispot.com/blog/revolutionizing-biotechnology-exploring-10-innovative-venture-backed-companies) .


US law now supports this change. The FDA Modernization Act 2.0 lets drug developers use alternatives to animal tests, such as cell-based assays and computer models, to support an application to start human trials ([Congress.gov, S.5002](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/senate-bill/5002) ). This change became law in the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, signed on 29 December 2022 ([Congress.gov, Public Law 117-328](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/2617) ). In September 2026, the FDA issued a direct final rule that updates its regulations. The rule makes clear that non-animal methods, such as organs-on-chips, can be used where appropriate to test drug safety before human trials ([FDA, 21 September 2026](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-updates-regulations-advance-innovative-alternatives-animal-testing) ).

### 1. Emulate


**CEO:** Jim Corbett | **Headquarters:** Boston, Massachusetts, USA


[Emulate](https://emulatebio.com/) makes Organ-Chips and the AVA Emulation System. Its founding team started the Organ-Chip work at the Wyss Institute at Harvard University. Donald Ingber is the scientific founder and Daniel Levner is a co-founder and the CTO. Emulate offers models such as the lung, liver, brain, intestine and kidney. In September 2026, Emulate submitted the full qualification package for its Human Liver-Chip to the FDA ISTAND program. This liver on a chip model helps researchers assess drug-induced liver injury.


### 2. InSphero


**CEO:** Jan Lichtenberg, PhD | **Headquarters:** Schlieren, Switzerland


[InSphero](https://insphero.com/) develops 3D microtissue models for drug discovery and safety tests. Jan Lichtenberg is the CEO and a co-founder. Wolfgang Moritz is also a co-founder. The company sells Akura microplate technology and Akura organ-on-chip technology. These tools help labs grow and test 3D human tissues at scale.


### 3. Elveflow


**CEO:** Jérémy Cramer, PhD | **Headquarters:** Paris, France


[Elveflow](https://elveflow.com/) is a brand of Elvesys SAS. It designs microfluidic instruments for pressure-driven flow control, flow measurement and valves. Organ-on-a-chip and dynamic cell perfusion are key applications. Its OB1 pressure controller controls the flow in microfluidic chips. Guilhem Velvé Casquillas, Mathieu Velvé Casquillas and Adrien Plecis founded the company. They are now advisors. Jérémy Cramer leads Elveflow and also leads Cherry Biotech (number 9 on this list).


### 4. Mimetas


**Co-CEOs:** Paul Vulto and Jos Joore | **Headquarters:** Leiden, the Netherlands


[Mimetas](https://www.mimetas.com/) started in 2013 in Leiden and in Gaithersburg, Maryland, USA. Its co-founders, Paul Vulto and Jos Joore, are the co-CEOs. The company makes the OrganoPlate platform. Mimetas says OrganoPlate is the first mass-produced, quality-controlled organ-on-a-chip platform. Researchers use it for gut, liver, kidney, blood vessel, blood-brain barrier, nervous system and lung models. In August 2026, Bruker made a majority investment in Mimetas. Mimetas keeps its own brand and management ([The Business of Biofabrication, 12 August 2026](https://businessofbiofabrication.com/2026/08/12/mimetas-bruker-majority-investment/) ).


### 5. MesoBioTech


**Co-founder:** Jian Shi | **Headquarters:** Paris, France


[MesoBioTech](https://mesobiotech.com/) started in May 2016 as a spin-off of ENS - PSL in Paris. It makes integrated microfluidic chips, flow controllers and culture patches with monolayer nanofibers. It also makes tissue patches from human pluripotent stem cells and organ-on-a-chip models. These products support stem cell research. For more companies in this field, read about the[top innovative stem cell companies in the US](https://www.scispot.com/blog/top-innovative-stem-cell-companies-in-the-us) .


### 6. Chiron


**Co-founder:** Dustin Dopsa | **Headquarters:** Maastricht, the Netherlands


[Chiron](https://www.chrn.co/) develops organ-on-chip technology for joint and tumour research. Its Re-Plate platform recreates human-like movement in vitro for arthritis research. Its μMass device helps labs grow 3D solid tumours. Chiron offers contract research services, device sales and consulting to pharmaceutical companies.


### 7. 28bio (formerly AxoSim)


**CEO:** Alif Saleh | **Headquarters:** Metairie (New Orleans area), Louisiana, USA


[28bio](https://www.28bio.com/) is the new name of AxoSim. The company changed its name in June 2025. It builds human brain organoids to predict how drugs affect the nervous system. Its platforms include CNS-3D Brain Organoids and the Nexon neurotechnology platform. Alif Saleh became CEO in June 2024. Co-founder Lowry Curley, PhD, was the CEO before him. For a related case, read how a lab[improved organoid drug discovery with Scispot](https://www.scispot.com/resources/accelerating-crispr-screening-workflows-how-bioinnovate-labs-anonymized-improved-organoid-drug-discovery-with-scispot) .


### 8. Valo Health


**CEO:** Brian Alexander, MD, MPH | **Headquarters:** Boston, Massachusetts, USA


[Valo Health](https://www.valohealth.com/) is a drug discovery company that Flagship Pioneering founded. It uses AI and human data to discover drugs. In 2022, Valo acquired TARA Biosystems and its human cardiac tissue models ([Valo Health, 5 April 2022](https://www.valohealth.com/press/valo-health-acquires-tara-biosystems-creating-first-of-its-kind-vertically-integrated-cardiovascular-platform) ). These heart tissue models help Valo test drug candidates for heart disease.


### 9. Cherry Biotech


**CEO:** Jérémy Cramer, PhD | **Headquarters:** Montreuil (Paris area), France


[Cherry Biotech](https://www.cherrybiotech.com/) started in 2014 in Rennes, France. It moved to Montreuil, near Paris, in 2020. Jérémy Cramer is a co-founder and the CEO. Guilhem Velvé Casquillas is a co-founder and board member. The company makes CubiX, a microenvironment controller for complex organ models. Cherry Biotech shares a building with 4Dcell.


### 10. 4Dcell


**CEO:** Cyril Cerveau | **Headquarters:** Montreuil (Paris area), France


[4Dcell](https://www.4dcell.com/) develops tools that control the physical environment of cells. Cyril Cerveau is the CEO and a co-founder. Maël Le Berre is the President and a co-founder. Its SmartHeart platform is a human 3D cardiac microtissue platform. 4Dcell works with pharmaceutical companies, biotech companies and research institutes.


### 11. CN Bio


**CEO:** Dr Paul Brooks | **Headquarters:** Cambridge, UK


[CN Bio](https://cn-bio.com/) makes the PhysioMimix range of organ-on-a-chip systems. These systems support single-organ and multi-organ models, such as liver on a chip, gut, lung and linked organ models. CN Bio reports a research collaboration with the FDA since 2017. Dr Paul Brooks joined CN Bio as CEO in 2022. The company is at Cambridge Science Park.


CN Bio replaces Nortis on this list. In October 2024, Quris-AI acquired the assets of Nortis, including its kidney-on-chip technology ([GlobeNewswire, 29 October 2024](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/10/29/2970665/0/en/quris-ai-acquires-nortis.html) ).


### 12. BioIVT


**CEO:** Dr Auro Nair | **Headquarters:** Woodbury, New York, USA


[BioIVT](https://bioivt.com/) supplies human and animal biospecimens, ADME-Tox products and research services for drug and diagnostic development ([BusinessWire, 2 February 2026](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260202739527/en/BioIVT-Appoints-Dr.-Auro-Nair-as-Chief-Executive-Officer) ). Labs use these human cells and tissues to build human-relevant test models. Dr Auro Nair became CEO in February 2026.


### 13. AlveoliX


**CEO:** Dr Nina Hobi | **Headquarters:** Bern, Switzerland


[AlveoliX](https://www.alveolix.com/) develops lung on a chip technology. Its AX Lung-on-Chip System recreates the breathing motion of the human lung. Dr Nina Hobi is the CEO and Scientific Director. In February 2026, AlveoliX helped to found the Industry Alliance for Microphysiological Systems (IAMPS) in Europe.


### 14. TissUse


**CEO:** Dr Reyk Horland | **Headquarters:** Berlin, Germany


[TissUse](https://www.tissuse.com/en/) developed the HUMIMIC Multi-Organ-Chip platform. This multi organ chip connects more than one human tissue in one circuit. Researchers use it to study how a drug acts across organs. Dr Uwe Marx is the scientific founder. Dr Reyk Horland became CEO in October 2020.


### 15. BEOnchip


**CEO:** Rosa Monge | **Headquarters:** Zaragoza, Spain


[BEOnchip](https://beonchip.com/) started in 2016 at the University of Zaragoza. Rosa Monge, Ignacio Ochoa and Luis Fernández founded it. Rosa Monge is the CEO and Head of R&D. The company makes standard and custom microfluidic chips, such as Be-Doubleflow, Be-Gradient and Be-Transflow. The company says that its chips make organ-on-chip simple to use.


### 16. BiomimX


**CEO:** Paola Occhetta, PhD | **Headquarters:** Milan, Italy


[BiomimX](https://www.biomimx.com/) develops organ-on-chip models with mechanical stimulation. Its patented uBeat technology applies controlled mechanical forces to microtissues, for example in a beating heart-on-chip model. Paola Occhetta is the CEO and a co-founder. Marco Rasponi is the CTO and a co-founder. Prof. Rasponi of Politecnico di Milano coordinates PHOENIX, a Horizon Europe project on organs-on-chip.


### 17. Tissue Dynamics


**CEO:** Dr Avner Ehrlich | **Headquarters:** Rehovot, Israel


[Tissue Dynamics](https://www.tissuedynamics.com/) is a human-focused CRO. It uses human organoids, real-time metabolic data and AI to predict drug effects. Its DynamiX platform tests more than 20,000 human organoids in parallel with embedded metabolic sensors. Prof. Yaakov Nahmias is the founder and CSO. In May 2026, Tissue Dynamics and Galmed started to build a human model of chronic cardiac fibrosis ([Galmed, 6 May 2026](https://galmedpharma.investorroom.com/2026-05-06-Tissue-Dynamics-and-Galmed-Pharmaceuticals-to-Develop-Human-Centered-Chronic-Cardiac-Fibrosis-Platform-to-Advance-Aramchol-Based-Therapeutics) ).


### 18. Altis Biosystems


**CEO:** Ben Scruggs, PhD | **Headquarters:** Durham, North Carolina, USA


[Altis Biosystems](https://www.altisbiosystems.com/) makes RepliGut models of the human intestine. The range includes RepliGut Planar, RepliGut Crypt and RepliGut Immune Co-Culture. The co-culture model pairs gut epithelium with immune cells to model inflammation. Ben Scruggs is the Chair and CEO.


### 19. Bi/ond


**CEO:** Dr Cinzia Silvestri | **Headquarters:** Delft, the Netherlands


Bi/ond is a spin-off of TU Delft. Nikolas Gaio, Cinzia Silvestri and William Solano founded it ([TU Delft, October 2017](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/eemcs/current/science-stories/stories/from-cleanroom-to-boardroom) ). Dr Cinzia Silvestri is the CEO and Nikolas Gaio is the CTO. Its inCHIPit chip has an open tissue well and perfusable channels for 3D tissues and organoids.


### 20. NETRI


**CEO:** Thibault Honegger | **Headquarters:** Lyon, France


[NETRI](https://netri.com/) uses human neurons as sensors to measure how compounds affect human biology. Its "Neurons as a Sensor" method uses compartmentalized microfluidic devices, such as NeoBentos MEA. NETRI applies this method to preclinical safety and to drug discovery. Thibault Honegger is the CEO and a co-founder. In 2026, NETRI won the Amgen x NSG BioLabs Golden Ticket in Singapore ([Amgen, July 2026](https://www.amgen.com.sg/media/press-releases/2026/07/netri-wins-2026-amgen-x-nsg-golden-ticket-for-its-proprietary-human-neurons-as-a-sensor-neurofluidics-platform) ).

## The Future of Organ-on-a-Chip Technology


Organ-on-a-chip technology changes how researchers test drugs and model disease. The demand for human-relevant disease models continues to grow. AI, automation and multi-organ systems help researchers make models that are more predictive and easier to scale.


Regulators also support this change. In April 2025, the FDA published a roadmap to reduce animal testing in nonclinical studies, starting with monoclonal antibodies. In April 2026, the FDA reported that it met its Year 1 goals for this roadmap ([FDA, New Approach Methodologies](https://www.fda.gov/science-research/science-and-research-special-topics/new-approach-methodologies-nams) ). Related fields also grow. Read about the[top innovative tissue engineering companies](https://www.scispot.com/blog/top-innovative-tissue-engineering-startups) and the[most innovative 3D bioprinting startups](https://www.scispot.com/blog/10-most-innovative-3d-bioprinting-startups-in-the-world-right-now) .


## Conclusion


Organ-on-a-chip technology grows fast. Grand View Research projects a market of USD 952.4 million by 2030. In 2026, the field also changed. AxoSim became 28bio, Bruker took a majority stake in Mimetas, and Quris-AI now holds the Nortis technology. US law and FDA regulations now recognize organs-on-chips as possible nonclinical tests. The top innovative organ on a chip companies in world give labs more human-relevant models. But these models produce complex data. Labs need good data management to make chip results reproducible.
